findings: plan_aggregate.cpp: the large perfect hash aggregate path is gated on general properties: total key bits ≤ 22, perfect_ht_threshold ≥ 12, estimated input ≥ slots/2, no aggregate state with a destructor, slots*(state+1)*(threads+1) ≤ max_memory/8, and no DELIM_SCAN in the child. None of these refer to particular tables, columns, literals or scale factors. Any dense integer GROUP BY with up to 4M keys qualifies.

perfect_aggregate_hashtable.cpp: lazy-init mode looks correct. AddChunkLazy initializes each slot exactly once, even when a key repeats within a chunk, and keeps the out-of-range check that throws on corrupt statistics. NULL groups still map to slot 0. CombineRange initializes new target slots before every CombineStates flush. ScanRange and Destroy visit only slots that are set. In non-lazy mode, group_is_set and the full init path are unchanged.

physical_perfecthash_aggregate.cpp: concurrency looks safe. Combine runs per stripe under per-stripe mutexes, and each thread allocates from its own local arena, which is then moved into the global table's stored_allocators under the global lock. Parallel source threads claim disjoint 64K-slot blocks through an atomic counter and each gets its own arena. Because aggregates with destructors are excluded, the local tables need no state teardown after the combine.

block_allocator.cpp: the fallback reuse cache only applies when the block pool is inactive or disabled, and only to block_size allocations. It holds at most min(256MB, memory_limit/32) and is drained in ThreadFlush (idle worker threads, after 0.5s), FlushAll (buffer-pool eviction and purge paths), Resize (when the pool is turned on), SetLimit and the destructor. That is a small, bounded amount of extra memory that is released under pressure, so this is not a hidden cost shift.

Minor: physical_perfecthash_aggregate.hpp changes the non-large SourceOrder from NO_ORDER to INSERTION_ORDER, which contradicts the claim that non-large paths are byte-identical. The source there is single-threaded, so results are not affected, but it is an unrelated change. It is not enough to reject.
